title: Embedding runtime normalization adapter and calibrated similarity-score audit
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Score semantics across embedding models and legacy clients are drifting in production. Some models return high-norm vectors (leading to inflated dot scores), others return near-unit vectors (making dot ~= cosine). Clients and rerankers expect stable scoring units; downstream thresholds and rankers break when the numeric range changes.

Goal: Implement a runtime-side Normalization Adapter that produces a calibrated, model-aware similarity_score for rerank and similarity endpoints. The adapter should: (1) preserve backward compatibility by defaulting to legacy numeric output, (2) offer a negotiated/opt-in calibrated output that maps model-specific dot/cosine values to a stable normalized score unit, and (3) add telemetry and audit tooling to detect regressions and client mismatch.

High-level approach:
- Introduce a "Normalization Adapter" in the scoring pipeline that runs immediately before final scoring is returned to the client. The adapter can operate in three modes: LEGACY (pass-through), STANDARDIZE (per-model per-batch z-score normalization of raw dot/cos values using running mean/std), and CALIBRATE (map normalized values to a 0..1 similarity_score using a logistic/CDF transform fitted from small per-model calibration sets).
- Persist lightweight calibration metadata with each model (calib_mean, calib_std, transform_type, last_updated) in model registry. The runtime will fetch and cache this metadata.
- Expose a per-request header and API parameter for clients: X-Redwood-Similarity-Mode: legacy | standardize | calibrated. Default behaviour remains legacy to preserve existing contracts.
- Provide a runtime flag and tenant feature-flag for safe rollout. Initially enable CALIBRATE only in internal canaries and a small percent of opt-in tenants.

Why this differs from existing shims: instead of simple norm clipping or forcing cosine/dot toggles, this adapter performs lightweight statistical calibration so that the output numeric unit (similarity_score) is stable across model families, sequence-length distributions, and quantization profiles. The transform is intentionally conservative (monotonic, bounded) to minimize changes to rank order while stabilizing decision thresholds.

Acceptance criteria:
- New scores are monotonic with respect to original similarity measure (no inversions in >99.99% of pairs in synthetic suite).
- Median rank-change for top-10 results < 1 position for non-adopting clients; for opt-in calibrated clients we expect rank changes as needed but quality metrics should improve (NDCG / MRR).
- End-to-end added latency at p95 < 2ms for the adapter on typical GPU-hosted path.
- Unit tests, integration tests, and a canary run completed with zero critical regressions recorded.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Calibration metadata stale or misfit for traffic distribution -> mitigate with rolling updates and online monitoring of calibration drift, plus a fallback to LEGACY on large drift.
- Risk: Clients relying on raw numeric ranges -> mitigate with default LEGACY mode and strong client communications + deprecation plan.
- Risk: Added CPU cost on hot paths -> optimize adapter with vectorized ops and cache per-model transforms; fall back to precomputed LUT for small quantized models.

Migration and rollout plan summary:
1) Implement adapter behind runtime feature flag (no customer-visible change).
2) Add header support and document API param in SDKs as experimental.
3) Enable CALIBRATE for internal tenants + testjobs (2 weeks).
4) Canary to 5% of alpha tenants with opt-in notice (4 weeks). Monitor regression metrics.
5) If stable, extend to self-serve opt-in in console and SDKs.
6) After 90 days of stable telemetry, consider announcing recommended mode for new models.
